info.name: IMS - Transactions screen
info.description:
# Transactions screen API

Every stock movement is one row of `/api/transactions/`. This collection follows the screen: log in, fill the form, record receipts, movements that need approval, district use and returns, then lists, stock and errors. Run it top to bottom against a **test** server; it passes ids between requests.

## Roles
| Variable | Role | Account |
|---|---|---|
| `token_dg` | DG PDMA (master) | approves warehouse movements and returns, refers and decides demands |
| `token_warehouse` | Storage location user at a **Warehouse** | records movements (wait for DG approval), issues demands |
| `token_district` | Storage location user at a **District** | uses its own stock, returns stock, decides return requests |
| `token_ndma` | NDMA | only NDMA-owned stock and demand lines referred to NDMA |
| `token_inspection` | Inspection team | approves status changes |

## Variables
`item`, `sub_cat`, `spec` = Boat / Fiberglass / 19 ft; `warehouse` = Lahore Warehouse (1), `warehouse2` = Muzaffargarh Warehouse (3), `district` = Lahore district (2), `district2` = Bahawalpur district (6). Change them to match the test data.

item.name: 00 Log in
item.description: One login per role used below. Set the usernames and `password` in the environment.

request.description:
Log in and keep the access token for the **dg** requests. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other call; refresh it with `POST /api/auth/refresh/ {"refresh": "..."}` when it expires.

The `user` object says what the screens should show: `role`, `storage_location_id` / `storage_location_name` (none for DG PDMA, NDMA and the inspection team) and `can_approve_demands`.

Log in and keep the access token for the **warehouse** requests. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other call; refresh it with `POST /api/auth/refresh/ {"refresh": "..."}` when it expires.

The `user` object says what the screens should show: `role`, `storage_location_id` / `storage_location_name` (none for DG PDMA, NDMA and the inspection team) and `can_approve_demands`.

Log in and keep the access token for the **district** requests. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other call; refresh it with `POST /api/auth/refresh/ {"refresh": "..."}` when it expires.

The `user` object says what the screens should show: `role`, `storage_location_id` / `storage_location_name` (none for DG PDMA, NDMA and the inspection team) and `can_approve_demands`.

Log in and keep the access token for the **ndma** requests. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other call; refresh it with `POST /api/auth/refresh/ {"refresh": "..."}` when it expires.

The `user` object says what the screens should show: `role`, `storage_location_id` / `storage_location_name` (none for DG PDMA, NDMA and the inspection team) and `can_approve_demands`.

Log in and keep the access token for the **inspection** requests. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other call; refresh it with `POST /api/auth/refresh/ {"refresh": "..."}` when it expires.

The `user` object says what the screens should show: `role`, `storage_location_id` / `storage_location_name` (none for DG PDMA, NDMA and the inspection team) and `can_approve_demands`.

Same `user` object as the login. Use it to pick the screen mode:
- `role` = `master` → DG PDMA: approval inbox, can record any warehouse movement directly.
- `role` = `location` → a warehouse or district user: their own storage location only.
- `role` = `ndma` → only NDMA stock (owner 2).
- `role` = `inspection` → only the status-change approval inbox.

item.name: 01 Form lookups
item.description:
Fill the transaction form's dropdowns. Lookups are readable by every logged-in user.

| Field | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `txn_type` | `/api/transaction-type/` | `direction` decides which location fields to show (see folder 02) |
| `status` | `/api/item-status/` | **required on every new line**: 1 Serviceable, 2 Non Serviceable |
| `condition` | `/api/item-condition/?status=<status>` | Serviceable: Ready to Use (filled in when left out); Non Serviceable: Repairable, Expired, Beyond Repair (required) |
| `shelf_life_months` | number | optional; with `manufacturing_date` it sets `expiry_date` when none is given |
| `owner` | `/api/stock-owner/` | 1 PDMA (default), 2 NDMA; only NDMA users record NDMA stock |
| `purpose` | `/api/dispatch-purpose/` | **required for a Dispatch to a department** |
| `party` | `/api/parties/?txn_type=<type>` | loads with the chosen type: supplier (Procurement), donor (Donation), NDMA (NDMA), department (Dispatch) |
| `item` → `sub_cat` → `spec` | `/api/items/` then `/api/items/<id>/options/` | choose sub category and spec when the item has them |
| storage locations | `/api/storage-location/` | `type_name` District / Warehouse decides what needs approval |
| sheds | `/api/storage-shed/?storage_location=<id>` | optional; a shed number (1 for Shed-1) is also accepted |

request.description:
| id | Type | direction | From → To | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Donation | in | → any | none |
| 2 | Procurement | in | → any | none |
| 3 | NDMA | in | → any | none |
| 6 | Opening Stock | in | → any | none |
| 4 | Dispatch | out | → a district (`to_storage_location`) or → a department (`party` + `purpose`) | warehouse: DG; district → district: DG; district → department: none; NDMA → PDMA: DG picks the warehouse |
| 5 | Internal Transfer | transfer | warehouse → warehouse, or shed → shed of one warehouse | DG PDMA |
| 9 | Return | transfer | district → warehouse; PDMA → NDMA (NDMA stock, no destination) | DG PDMA |
| 7 | Status Change | status | same location, `from_status` → `status` | Inspection team |

Movements recorded by the DG PDMA, receipts, a district's Dispatch to a department and issues against approved demands are approved at once.
Serviceable (1), Non Serviceable (2).

Second level under the status: load it when the user picks the status. Serviceable has Ready to Use (filled in automatically); Non Serviceable has Repairable, Expired and Beyond Repair (one must be chosen).
PDMA (1) and NDMA (2).
Required `purpose` of a Dispatch to a department.
Parties load with the chosen type. For Dispatch the user chooses **District** (show districts from `/api/storage-location/`, `type_name` District) or **Department** (show this list).
`?item_category=<id>` narrows by category. Each item has `unit_name`.
All dropdown data for one item: `sub_categories[]` each with `specs[]`, plus item-wide `specs[]`. Also `/api/items/<id>/sub-categories/` and `/api/items/<id>/specs/?sub_category=<id>`.
Every user sees all (e.g. to choose where to send). `type_name` is District or Warehouse.
Sheds to choose for `from_sto_shed` / `to_sto_shed`.

item.name: 02 Receipts (no approval)
item.description:
Incoming types fill `to_storage_location` (a storage location user may leave it out: it is their own).
They are approved at once. `party` is required for Procurement (supplier), Donation (donor) and NDMA.

request.description: Suppliers, donors and NDMA are one list, each under its transaction type. Names are unique per type.

Response has every id plus names: `txn_type_name`, `item_name`, `sub_cat_name`, `spec_name`, `status_name`, `owner_name`, `party_name`, `to_storage_location_name`, `approval_status` (approved for receipts) and `picture` / `receipt` (URLs or null).

Send as **multipart/form-data** to attach images: `picture` (the goods) and `receipt`. They are stored as JPEG and returned as URLs (`/api/transactions/<id>/picture/`), which need the Authorization header: fetch them with the token and show them as a blob URL. Send an empty value to remove an image (PATCH).
The image itself (image/jpeg). Same for `/receipt/`.

item.name: Receipt with shelf life (expiry worked out)

request.description: `shelf_life_months` with `manufacturing_date` sets `expiry_date` (here 2027-07-15) when none is given.

item.name: Non Serviceable receipt needs a condition

request.description: `{"condition": ["Choose the condition of the Non Serviceable stock."]}`
Master users have no own location, so they always give `to_storage_location`.
POST a JSON list to save several item lines together: all or nothing. Lists are JSON only (attach images per line afterwards with PATCH multipart).

item.name: 03 Warehouse movements (DG PDMA approval)
item.description:
A warehouse user's Internal Transfer, Dispatch to District or Dispatch is saved with `approval_status` **pending**:
it changes no stock until approved but already holds the quantity at the sender. The DG's own movements are approved at once.
Show a "Pending approval" badge; the sender can still edit or delete a pending movement.

item.name: Dispatch to a district (warehouse user) → pending

request.description: Warehouse → district. `from_storage_location` defaults to the user's own warehouse.
Shifting, only between warehouses. Shed to shed inside one warehouse: same `to_storage_location` as the sender with a different `to_sto_shed` (and `from_sto_shed`).
Pending movements the logged-in user can approve: the DG sees everything but status changes; the inspection team only status changes. Also `?approval_status=pending|approved|rejected` on any list.
`approval_remarks` optional. Stock moves now. The response is the updated transaction (`approved_by`, `approved_at`).
Rejected movements stay in the list (`approval_status` rejected) and never count.

item.name: DG sends directly → approved at once

request.description: The DG can send PDMA stock from any warehouse to any location without a demand.

item.name: Warehouse dispatches to a department → pending

request.description: Department = a party of the Dispatch type; `purpose` required; stock leaves the system once approved.
Only the DG PDMA (and the inspection team for status changes) see approve/reject buttons.

item.name: 04 District use, status changes and returns
item.description:
A district manages its own stock: its Dispatch needs a `purpose` and no approval.
Status changes wait for the inspection team. Returns (district → warehouse) wait for the DG and should be split by status.

item.name: District dispatch to a department (no approval)

request.description: `party` (department) and `purpose` required; `issued_to` optional. Stock leaves the system.

item.name: District dispatch to another district → pending (DG)

request.description: A district may send to another district; it waits for the DG PDMA.

Status Change: (`from_status`, `from_condition`) now → (`status`, `condition`) new, at one location; the sending location defaults to the user's own and `from_condition` is filled in when the old status has one condition. Waits for the inspection team. Attach a damage picture with multipart if needed.
The inspection team only sees status changes.
Stock moves from Serviceable to Repairable.
Return = district → warehouse; one line per status. Waits for the DG.
Approve each line.
Approve each line.

item.name: 05 Lists, edits and deletes
item.description:
Lists are newest first and limited to what the user may see (their location; NDMA its stock; inspection its status changes).
Filters: `txn_type`, `direction` (in/out/transfer/status), `party`, `owner`, `item`, `sub_category`, `spec`, `status`,
`storage_location`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `approval_status`, `awaiting_my_approval=true`.

request.description: Each row shows `direction`, `approval_status` and names.

item.name: Filter: pending transfers of an item
Edit an approved warehouse movement → pending again

request.description: A change by the warehouse to a movement that needs approval needs approval again. Refused with a `quantity` error when the receiver has already used the stock it delivered.

item.name: Warehouse cannot delete an approved movement

request.description: Only whoever approves it removes an approved movement; pending ones the sender deletes (204).

item.name: 06 Stock and reports
item.description: Stock is computed from approved transactions, per storage location, shed, item, sub category, spec, status and owner.

request.description: Filters: `storage_location`, `shed`, `item`, `sub_category`, `spec`, `status`, `condition`, `owner`, `category`.
Totals per item, sub category, spec, status, condition and owner.

Counts approved movements only unless `approval_status` is given. Breakdowns: `by_type`, `by_status`, `by_owner`, `by_condition`, `by_party`, `by_category`, `by_storage_location`, `by_item`, `by_item_variant`, `by_month`.

item.name: 07 NDMA stock
item.description: NDMA users see and record only NDMA-owned stock (owner 2), kept in any PDMA storage location.

item.name: NDMA receives its stock at a PDMA warehouse

request.description: `owner` defaults to 2 for NDMA users; NDMA has no own location, so `to_storage_location` is required.
Only owner 2 rows.

item.name: NDMA dispatches stock to PDMA (no warehouse)

request.description: NDMA stock goes only to PDMA warehouses and the DG PDMA picks which: leave `to_storage_location` empty (or suggest one). It waits for the DG; `from_owner` 2 → `owner` 1.

item.name: DG approves and picks the warehouse

request.description: For NDMA stock sent to PDMA, approve with `to_storage_location` (a warehouse) and optionally `to_sto_shed`. The stock becomes PDMA's there.

item.name: Warehouse returns NDMA stock to NDMA → pending

request.description: Return with `owner` 2 and no destination sends NDMA stock back to NDMA; the DG PDMA approves.

item.name: DG approves the return to NDMA
PDMA users cannot record NDMA stock
08 Validation errors to show
item.description: Errors come back as HTTP 400 `{"field": ["message"]}` (or `{"detail": "..."}` for 403/404). Show them next to the field.

request.description: `{"status": ["This field is required."]}`

item.name: Missing sub category of an item that has them

request.description: `{"sub_cat": ["Choose a sub category of this item."]}`
`{"quantity": "Not enough stock at ..."}`

item.name: Wrong movement type (Internal Transfer to a district)

request.description: `{"txn_type": [...]}` explains which type to use.
District stock is the district's; the DG asks for returns through demands.

item.name: Dispatch needs a district or a department

request.description: `{"to_storage_location": ["Choose the district or the department it goes to."]}`
